standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of the zero scheme of a section
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Divisors, label divisors-definition-zero-scheme-s, invoked at proof line 4221
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the ideal sheaf cutting out the zero scheme at the generic point of a component with the principal ideal generated by the local expression of the section.

core_obligations: Compare coefficients: for an integral closed subscheme of codimension one with generic point, choose a generator of the invertible sheaf there and write the section as an element f of the local ring (proof lines 4215-4219).

Identify the two lengths: the ideal of the zero scheme at that point is generated by f, so the length of the local ring of the zero scheme equals the length of the quotient by f, which is by definition the order of f (proof lines 4220-4229).
Read off the second statement from the first, since the divisor of the section and the cap with the first Chern class agree by construction (proof lines 4206-4211).
proof_roadmap: Coefficient comparison at the generic point (proof lines 4215-4219).
Second statement from the first (proof lines 4206-4211).
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes the divisor of a nonzero global section of an invertible sheaf as the cycle class of its zero scheme, and the same for the cap with the first Chern class (statement lines 4197-4213, tag 02SL-adjacent). The proof compares coefficients at the generic point of a codimension one component, choosing a local generator so that the section becomes an element of the local ring, and identifies the length of the zero scheme there with the order of that element. The coefficient comparison is the substance, so the claim is H2.
